title: Identify the intermittent real-form activation boundary before repair
why: The observed intermittent timeout occurs inside the real browser email/password journey; only the browser-tests workload covers the full activation and navigation contract.
coverage: docs/validation/manifest.json tiers.test-heavy browser-tests selects tests/clerk-sign-in-navigation.spec.ts and the existing phone readiness cases, together with typecheck, unit-tests and release-schema-contract inside the existing 900000 ms budget. Supported file/case diagnostics supplement, never replace, the full workload.
scope:
Prepared amendment candidate for the same admitted diagnostic identity ff5f011e-7a04-45c8-a9f4-3792cf7e471f; NOT applied, sealed or implemented. Preserve its current diagnostic revision and all run evidence. Run cf4c9bae-77ad-479f-bd97-36c3c7c33315 on chromium executed the real form then failed at tests/clerk-sign-in-navigation.spec.ts:71 with TimeoutError: page.waitForFunction: Timeout 30000ms exceeded. Its isolated retry passed all existing assertions; this establishes intermittency, not a cause or pre-existing provenance. The provider/challenge/session boundary remains unresolved. No routing or local authorization defect is established.

Before instrumentation or repair, apply this candidate through gate:amend against that SAME identity with an accurate reason and authorization applicability, then run gate:guard --tier test-heavy. Reconcile actual current source, plan revision and workload first. This candidate is preparation only; it does not retroactively authorize or claim implementation.

Concrete next diagnostic steps: instrument only this real-form case and its helper, without changing inputs, waits, assertions, context isolation or challenge submission behavior. Track an allow-listed stage, elapsed milliseconds, whether the optional challenge was observed within its existing 12-second window and whether one submission was attempted. On failure collect only Clerk loaded/session-present booleans, challenge-visible boolean, an allow-listed coarse sign-in status if supported, and a classified pathname with query/fragment removed. Limit collection to 2 seconds, output to 2 KiB; collector or logger failures must preserve the original error. Never retain submitted credentials or codes, tokens, cookies, storage state, user/session IDs, arbitrary DOM/provider text, full URLs or request/response bodies. Do not add traces or change retry policy. Add detecting privacy/deadline tests before collecting real-provider diagnostics. Use the supported file/case selector to rerun the original journey once with the bounded evidence.

Repair decision boundary: only if evidence shows the optional challenge observation ended without submission while a supported challenge remained visible during the later activation timeout, admit the smallest test-local challenge/session coordinator in a further same-task amendment. Plan one finite 30-second activation deadline, observe session and challenge together, submit each observed challenge once, tolerate auto-disappearing accepted controls, and stop after activation/context closure. Detect late challenge after 12 seconds, immediate no-challenge activation, auto-submitted disappearance, never-completing challenge, terminal failure and context closure with deterministic controlled ordering; assert exactly one or zero submissions and finite termination. If evidence instead identifies a provider prerequisite, report that blocker without a test workaround. If production lifecycle is implicated, prepare a separate concrete supported same-task scope amendment and affected-boundary assertions before changing it. An activation timeout alone does not authorize any of those repairs. No blind timeout increase, password resubmission, reload, ticket substitution, forced navigation, SDK upgrade or routing change is admitted.

Keep the existing real-form assertions for active session, automatic exact Settings URL, protected Settings title and local-user HTTP 200; keep empty browser storage, testing-token routing and finally context.close. Preserve both phone delayed-readiness cases and exact click histories. Run the complete bound heavy tier after any admitted coherent change. Record original failure and every retry separately with target/revision/actual commands and gaps. No baseline exclusions, gate maintenance, production deployment, independent verification or photo/upload/image/WebSocket repair is included.

approval.reference: Assigned diagnostic task 997 and its explicit instruction to prepare an evidence-scoped same-task amendment before necessary diagnostic instrumentation or material repair.
approval.direction: Preparation of this candidate is covered; do not apply speculative behavior repairs. Establish exact responsible-boundary evidence first.
approval.applicability: This file records a proposed next diagnostic boundary, not an implementation authorization, sealed amendment or new task. Check actual authorization and apply through the same-task amendment route before execution.

assertions.requirement: R1: Retain the decisive real-form contract
assertions.check: tests/clerk-sign-in-navigation.spec.ts signed-out Settings entry returns to protected Settings after form sign-in retains empty browser context, actual email/password/challenge, active Clerk session, automatic exact Settings destination, visible Settings title and local-user HTTP 200. Original failed activation stage and isolated passing retry remain distinct.

assertions.requirement: R2: Failure diagnostics are bounded and cannot disclose inputs or mask the original error
assertions.check: Planned deterministic tests in tests/clerk-sign-in-navigation.spec.ts at the diagnostics helper boundary inject credential/code/token/cookie/ID/provider-text sentinels and URL queries/fragments; require output to contain only allow-listed stage, coarse status, booleans, bounded elapsed value and classified pathname, at most 2 KiB. Hanging/throwing collectors and throwing loggers must preserve the same original error within the 2-second collection cap; no diagnostic collection after context closure.

assertions.requirement: R3: Any actual repair requires decisive evidence and a further same-task amendment
assertions.check: Before changing challenge behavior, require the missed-observation/visible-unsubmitted-challenge evidence defined in scope. A subsequently admitted coordinator must have controlled late-challenge, no-challenge, disappearing-control, persistent-failure and context-close cases in tests/clerk-sign-in-navigation.spec.ts asserting submission counts and finite termination. If evidence does not support this boundary, do not implement this proposed coordinator.

tests/mobile-photo-upload.spec.ts both existing delayed session readiness cases on mobile-chromium require active capture, aisle control and click histories exactly [] or [Mobile Flow], including idempotent re-entry. Keep downstream filename/photo assertions outside repair scope.

regression.rationale: A future implementation of failure instrumentation affects privacy and error-path reliability; the current file only prepares it. Normal detecting coverage is required before any such change, and a further amendment is required before a challenge/session behavior repair.
regression.covers: Failure diagnostics must never expose credentials, verification inputs, identities, cookies, tokens or arbitrary provider payloads, exceed the collection/output budget, continue after closure, or replace the original sign-in failure.
regression.testLocation: tests/clerk-sign-in-navigation.spec.ts planned diagnostic redaction, timeout, collector/logger failure and context-close cases
regression.assertion: Inject sensitive sentinels and URL query/fragment text; assert allow-listed output only, maximum 2 KiB, maximum 2 seconds, exact preservation of the original failure and no post-closure collection. Existing real-form assertions continue to distinguish activation, automatic navigation, protected rendering and local-user HTTP 200.
